entry-generation: Construction rejects a negative capacity with IllegalArgumentException through Assert.isTrue, stores the supplied capacity and generator, and initializes a ConcurrentHashMap plus read/write maintenance structures. Zero is accepted. The task assumes non-null keys and a non-null generator; invalid-key or null-generator behavior is outside scope.

With capacity zero, every get directly returns generator.apply(key), bypassing map lookup, insertion and read/write maintenance. No value is cached; a null result is returned directly because this branch does not reach insertion's value assertion.

With positive capacity, get first looks up the map. A hit records a read on that node and returns its stored value. A miss invokes the generator, calls the private insertion helper, then returns the locally generated value. Generation is not performed under the eviction lock or by computeIfAbsent.

Insertion validates key and value, creates a node with an ACTIVE entry and uses putIfAbsent. A successful insertion schedules an addition task; a losing insertion records a read on the prior node. Competing misses may run the generator more than once, and a losing get still returns its own generated value rather than replacing it with the winner's cached value; there is no single-flight or shared-result guarantee.

For positive capacity a null generated value is rejected with IllegalArgumentException by Assert.notNull before putIfAbsent, even if another thread has meanwhile inserted that key. Generator exceptions are not caught or translated here and prevent this invocation from reaching insertion; do not claim that they remove another thread's existing entry or that null results are cached.
read-recency: Hits and losing putIfAbsent attempts call processRead. recordRead chooses one of four buffers from the current thread ID and writes the node into a 128-slot ring using the recorded-count position, advancing the recorded count. This is buffered access recording, not a direct queue move on each hit.

recordRead computes pending as the captured pre-increment recorded count minus processed count and returns whether pending is less than 32. True means the read can be delayed, despite the processRead local variable's name; the drain-status policy determines whether to attempt a drain.

A read drain visits all four buffers, starting from the current thread's stripe. Each buffer processes at most 64 positions and stops on a null slot; it clears a consumed slot, asks the eviction queue to move that node to the back and advances readCount. After that loop it sets processedCount to the recorded-count snapshot, not merely to the number of nodes actually moved.

moveToBack only unlinks and re-appends a node already present in the eviction queue and not already last; a missing node is not resurrected and a last node is unchanged. Bounded, deferred ring recording is not a guarantee of a distinct synchronous globally ordered recency update for every concurrent access; eviction follows the maintained queue rather than an instantaneous total order of all get calls.
drain-coordination: processWrite appends a Runnable to the concurrent write queue, sets drain status REQUIRED and calls drainOperations. Maintenance is attempted by the calling operation; this code does not create a background worker or timer to drain pending tasks.

The read-side status policy is: IDLE requests a drain only when the read is not delayable, REQUIRED always requests a drain, and PROCESSING does not request another read-triggered drain. If tryLock fails, drainOperations returns without draining or waiting; pending work can remain for another operation to attempt.

On successful tryLock, draining sets PROCESSING, drains reads first and then at most 16 write tasks, stopping early if the write queue is empty. This normal drain is distinct from clear's drainAll. The eviction lock serializes maintenance, not generator execution or every concurrent-map get/put/remove.

A finally block compare-and-sets PROCESSING to IDLE and unlocks. If a writer has changed the status to REQUIRED during processing, the conditional reset does not overwrite that request. Unlock is attempted even if draining propagates an exception; do not claim that one normal drain necessarily empties all pending work.
insertion-eviction: The concurrent map can contain the new node before its AddTask runs. AddTask increments internal currentSize even if the node is no longer ACTIVE, but only an ACTIVE node is added to the eviction queue and triggers that task's eviction loop. Queue insertion puts a not-already-present node at the back and avoids duplicate membership.

The eviction loop runs while currentSize exceeds capacity, polling the queue front, which is its least-recently-used end. An empty queue makes the loop return. For a polled node it removes the map entry using both key and that node, then marks the node removed; this conditional removal does not blindly delete a newer replacement under the same key.

markAsRemoved retries a CAS replacing the node's entry with a REMOVED entry that retains the value, and decrements currentSize after the successful CAS. This bookkeeping follows node/task processing; it is not a direct call to the map's size and does not destroy or clear the stored value.

Map mutation and deferred accounting/queue maintenance are separate. Under contention the backing map can temporarily exceed capacity before maintenance catches up, and eviction uses buffered recency. Do not promise immediate strict map-size enforcement or a globally exact per-access LRU order. The ordinary sequential insertion test demonstrates bounded eviction in its tested scenario, not those stronger concurrent guarantees.
key-removal: remove first removes the key from the concurrent map. If no node was present it returns false without scheduling removal work. Otherwise it marks the node for removal, enqueues a RemovalTask via processWrite, and returns true; map visibility changes before deferred queue/accounting cleanup.

markForRemoval loops over the node's entry. A non-ACTIVE entry returns unchanged; an ACTIVE entry is replaced by a PENDING_REMOVAL entry retaining its value through CAS, retrying on contention. It does not unconditionally overwrite an already removed state.

RemovalTask removes queue membership if present and then calls markAsRemoved for REMOVED-state/accounting cleanup. This task uses the ordinary buffered write/drain path and can be deferred when the eviction lock is unavailable. Existing holders still have a node whose value is retained, so map removal does not retroactively cancel a get that already obtained that node.
clear-and-observation: clear takes the eviction lock with blocking lock(), unlike ordinary tryLock maintenance, and unlocks in finally. It repeatedly polls queued nodes, removes each map association conditionally by key and node, and marks each polled node removed with accounting cleanup.

After polling the eviction queue, clear clears all read-buffer slots and then drains all queued write tasks until the queue is empty, not just the normal 16-task limit. ReadOperations.clear nulls slots without resetting its recorded/read/processed counters. The sequence is queue removal, read-slot clearing, then write-task execution; it is not a direct cache.clear().

The eviction lock does not exclude all concurrent map mutations, and a pending AddTask can run during the final write drain after the initial eviction-queue removal loop. Therefore do not claim that clear is an unconditional atomic empty-map barrier for arbitrary concurrent or pending operations. Explain the source ordering rather than extrapolating the Javadoc or sequential tests into a stronger concurrency guarantee.

size returns concurrent-map size and contains tests concurrent-map key membership, whereas capacity and deprecated sizeLimit return the configured capacity. These are distinct from deferred currentSize accounting. Existing tests corroborate zero-capacity nonretention, sequential insertion/eviction, removal, and clear followed by reuse; they do not establish single-flight generation, per-hit globally exact LRU, or atomic clearing under contention.
